Third Mark of the Afternoon Sun, catching the dripping water from the eaves—each drop weighs one zhu, falling from a height of nine chi.  
Over twenty-four years, the dripping water could carve a hole three cun and seven fen deep.  
Then…  
"The size of a shadow depends on the tilt, distance, and alignment."  
By this measure, this inverted shadow should be visible to three of us on my return to the mountain.  

Before I left to wander the world, I already felt insignificant, lost on the path to the heavens. I leave you this "Thousand Days of Drops" test, a reflection of my hopes. Beyond these mountains, perhaps something extraordinary awaits.  
Now, en route to Hutuo, I am struck by a thought: Wherever I am needed, there I shall go—such is the fleeting yet meaningful nature of life.
